text.p: Concern that the goal of first-tier European economic and monetary union (EMU) is once more slipping beyond Italy's reach took a weighty toll on its debt markets.

While cash bonds were nearly one point off on the day, futures shed 130 basis points, the benchmark bond spread over the benchmark Bund yawned to 161 basis points from around about 150 on Friday and the lira spiralled to 989.00 per mark.

"All the news from the Davos economic meeting, with business leaders saying they don't want Italy in the first wave, and then waiting for the Eurostat news -- all that combined to weigh Btps down," one broker in London said.
The March future on LIFFE was 134 basis points down at 129.24 with next support at 128.96 and resistance at 129.40.

The November 2006 Btp was 79 basis points off at 103.77, yielding 7.33 percent and with a spread gaping to 161 basis points from around 150 on Friday. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 97 basis points off at 109.02.

The EU's statistics office Eurostat said a review of budget accounting procedures nipped 0.26 percent off Italy's 1997 deficit. A decision on its Euro tax is due by the month end and a trader said, "No news is bad news. It doesn't bode well, it means they're still trying to arrange something political."

"The convergence trend on Italy and Spain seems to be over for now," the broker said. He expected investors would pull more money from Btps now and noted the extent of the future's rally had been such that investors would still make good profits if they got out at these levels below the recent highs.
On the charts, a break at 128.96 would open the way to the 127 area, which meant the market would then be likely to test the 126.85 low of this year, seen in early January.
On the home front, final January consumer prices are due on Tuesday, with preliminary data putting it month-on-month at 0.2 pct and 2.6 pct year on year.-C.Cooper, Milan 00392 66129507
